project.project_title: Logo needed for UK start up catering company

source_message.speaker: client
source_message.text: Hi, before you begin developing concepts, we’ll send over some concepts that appeal to us, though naturally we also want to see your own ideas. Please hold off on starting the concepts until we’ve got back to you. Thanks, [CLIENT_NAME_001]

source_message.speaker: freelancer
source_message.text: Understood. I’ll develop a few concepts that closely reflect your vision, while introducing a creative element so the designs remain unique and visually appealing.

source_message.speaker: freelancer
source_message.text:
Hi [CLIENT_NAME_001], please review the initial drafts and share your thoughts with me. I’d be very interested to receive your feedback.

If you want any revisions, refinements, iterations, or changes, please feel free to say so. I’m happy to continue working with you until the result aligns perfectly with your vision.

execution.observed_behavior: Freelancer presents the initial logo drafts for client review.

source_message.speaker: client
source_message.text:
Thank you for these. We like the graduated orange colour and the lines beside the strapline.

Our preferences are the 1st and 3rd one, since the font used in the 2nd one feels too plain. However, someone unfamiliar with our name might not understand that the flame in the 3rd one represents an ‘O’, even though we like it.

Perhaps the flame could sit inside an ‘O’, be reshaped to look more like an ‘O’, or be superimposed over an ‘O’. Could you test all of those suggestions?

For logo 3, could we also see how it looks with ‘dough’ made slightly larger? To make the strapline more prominent, could you either outline every letter with a thin black pencil line or slightly brighten the orange tones used in the strapline lettering? We like the global dough font because it has character, particularly the G. We wondered whether a little ‘character’ could be added to a couple of the other letters, but thought it would be better to handle the revisions one stage at a time, as the existing font may be okay. Thank you—we’re moving in the right direction.

execution.observed_behavior: Client evaluates three delivered initial concepts, identifies preferred options, and confirms that the design process is moving in the right direction.

source_message.speaker: client
source_message.text: Hi, [FREELANCER_NAME_001] attached a draft logo made using AI—we were obviously only tinkering around with chat gpt. That said, we want fresh, original ideas, which is why we posted our proposal, although we do like those colours because they fit the look and feel of the Global Dough truck. The company is called 'Global Dough', so the logo should not contain the word 'truck'. The 'truck' component is only one area of the business. Put another way, 'Global Dough', the business needing the logo, will run a mobile catering truck, sell food online, and may also sell to other caterers/kitchens. This is why the business name is simply 'Global Dough', while the strapline stays the same. Are you happy to discuss anything before accepting the offer?

source_message.speaker: client
source_message.text:
Hi, apologies for taking so long to respond.

Matt prefers number 4, where the strapline matches the colour of ‘global’ and both use graduated colours.

I was wondering, though, whether you could add a little more character to the ‘global dough’ font. The food will be genuinely authentic and freshly cooked, featuring flavours from around the world. I like the unusual shape of the ‘G’ in both words; could a similar treatment be applied to more letters without taking it too far? thanks, [CLIENT_NAME_001]

value_updates.color_treatment: The strapline and ‘global’ both use matching graduated colors
value_updates.typography_style: Apply the distinctive treatment used for the G to additional letters without taking it too far

source_message.speaker: freelancer
source_message.text:
I think these two options represent roughly the greatest amount of character that can be introduced without harming the logo’s overall readability and quality. Adding more than this would begin to undermine the clean, refined appearance and reduce its versatility across different uses.

My focus has been on bringing subtle personality into the letterforms while retaining the brand’s premium and authentic feel. In my view, this adds a distinctive quality without sacrificing the logo’s professionalism or overall balance.

execution.observed_behavior: Freelancer reports producing two characterful letterform options while preserving readability, cleanliness, professionalism, and balance.

source_message.speaker: client
source_message.text:
Hi, thanks for these. We’re nearly there!
1\. For the second logo, please reduce the size of the U and the H so they match the height of all the other letters in ‘ DOUGH’.
2\. Could you flip the top on the right hand side of the H in DOUGH, making it mirror the top of the U in DOUGH?
3\. Lastly, could you apply the same feature to the top of the D in DOUGH, similar to the top of the B in GLOBAL?
Please refer to the attached annotated screenshot.
After that, we’ll review it again and hopefully it will retain the ‘clean’ appearance while also having the character.
Many thanks, [CLIENT_NAME_001]

value_updates.h_top_treatment: Flip the top-right of the H to mirror the top of the U
value_updates.d_top_treatment: Apply a feature to the top of the D similar to the top of the B in ‘GLOBAL’
value_updates.appearance_balance: Retain a clean appearance while adding character

source_message.speaker: client
source_message.text:
Hi, oops—I thought I had already replied!

We’d like to proceed with the agreed final version shown above, rev4-02. Thank you!

Am I correct in assuming that the logo will be supplied both with and without the black box, since a black box will not be suitable for every use?

Thank you, [CLIENT_NAME_001]

source_message.speaker: freelancer
source_message.text:
Hi [CLIENT_NAME_001], excellent! When convenient, could you approve the first milestone and activate the second, allowing me to proceed with the outstanding work?

Yes, the logo will be supplied with the black box and without it.

For the color variants, are you requesting every color version considered during the design process, or only the standard full-color, black, and white versions?

I’ll provide all required file formats as well, including fully editable source files, enabling you to use the logo for print, web, social media, signage, merchandise, and any other purpose. The final delivery will also contain the font information and color codes used in the chosen design.

I did want to clarify that logo guidelines were not part of the original project scope, as they are generally supplied through a separate project.

There are two options:

Basic Logo Usage Guidelines – $100
Covers logo variations, clear space, minimum size, color palette, typography, and basic do's and don'ts.

Complete Brand Guidelines – $150
Contains everything offered in the basic guide, along with a broader brand system addressing typography hierarchy, imagery style, iconography, layout principles, brand applications, stationery and t-shirt mockups, and detailed usage rules.

I’d be happy to produce either option if you wish, helping ensure the logo is applied consistently and professionally to all future branding materials.

Let me know if you'd like me to recommend a few font options.
